exact_statement: Let b be a prime. Prove an all-parameter support-minimal unequal-cardinality equal-product relation on distinct integers inside a fixed multiplicative tail (b^K/C_b,b^K], with logarithmic support and an ordered path prime-incidence graph, and use it to determine whether every o(N) deletion rule built from a lower threshold and sparse bounded prime-valuation observations must fail to hit some bad support. Any theorem must state the observation model exactly and must not claim tau(H_N)=o(N), an integral lower bound, or resolution of Erdos 786.
scope_notes: Variant lock: the two shores are disjoint Finsets of distinct positive integers; after cancellation every coefficient is in {-1,0,1}.

The fixed-width target is uniform in every sufficiently large exponent K for N=b^K. The multiplicative constant may be absolute or may depend only on b, but not on K, the controlled-prime set, or the relation.

The controlled valuation observation must be frozen before the counterexample is chosen. A permitted growing controlled-prime set P_K must omit b, lie below the declared roughness cutoff, and have a quantitative positive-density zero-signature cell.

A valuation-cylinder rule means that outside a lower threshold, deletion membership is constant on every vector (nu_p(n))_{p in P_K}; the theorem may refute this class only and must not be summarized as refuting every local, adaptive, largest-prime, or residue-aware rule.
The desired corollary is subsequence-valid at N=b^K and is enough to refute a rule claimed to work for every sufficiently large N. It does not imply a lower bound on tau(H_N).

The previous IR.1 and RR.1--RR.3 campaigns are read-only inputs identified below by file hashes. This campaign may strengthen or combine their scoped obstruction interfaces but may not rewrite their artifacts.
Public search for a solution of Erdos 786 is prohibited by the predecessor closure contracts. Ordinary named background such as Bertrand's postulate and elementary density estimates is allowed.

variant_lock.relation: disjoint finite shores with equal products and unequal cardinalities
variant_lock.minimality: no proper nonempty signed subrelation on the displayed support
variant_lock.forbidden: multisets, repeated vertices, arbitrary integer coefficients, or equality only after asymptotic approximation

frozen_observation_model.controlled_primes: P_K is finite, b is not in P_K, max(P_K)<b^floor(K/16), and sum_{p in P_K} 1/p <= 1-delta for one fixed delta>0
frozen_observation_model.cylinder_rule: outside [1,t_K], deletion is membership in a set A_K of complete sigma_K fibres
frozen_observation_model.success_to_refute: the resulting deletion is o(N) and meets every bad support for every sufficiently large N

read_only_dependencies.result: IR.1 moving power-thin support-minimal path relation
RR.1 ordered rough path and RR.2 universal residue extension
